subject: Astronomy & Space
title: Starshades and Coronagraphs
description: A fast breakdown of Starshades and Coronagraphs for builders.

hook.text: To see an exoplanet next to its star, you must block the star's blinding light. Two technologies compete for this job.

buildup.text: A coronagraph sits inside the telescope and blocks light internally. A starshade flies in space tens of thousands of km ahead.

discovery.text: Coronagraphs have improved a millionfold since the 1930s. Modern ones can suppress starlight by a factor of 10 billion.

twist.text: A starshade must maintain alignment with a distant telescope to within one meter—while both are thousands of km apart.

climax.text: Both approaches are being developed. Whichever succeeds could enable the first true photograph of an Earth-like world.

punchline.text: Block the star, see the planet. Two ideas racing to reveal alien Earths.

quiz.question: What is the main challenge of using a starshade?
options: It must maintain precise alignment with the telescope from thousands of kilometers away
It blocks all light, making it impossible to see the planet too
It can only be used once before needing replacement

details.summary: Starshades and coronagraphs are technologies designed to block a star's overwhelming light so exoplanets can be directly imaged. Coronagraphs sit inside the telescope, while starshades fly separately in formation, casting a shadow.
details.whyItMatters: Direct imaging of Earth-like exoplanets requires blocking starlight 10 billion times brighter than the planet. These technologies are essential for future missions aiming to photograph and characterize habitable worlds.
takeaways: Block starlight to reveal nearby exoplanets directly
Coronagraphs work internally; starshades fly in formation
Essential for imaging Earth-like planets in the future

faq.question: How does a starshade work?
faq.answer: A starshade is a large, flower-shaped spacecraft that flies tens of thousands of kilometers in front of a space telescope, blocking the target star's light while allowing planet light to pass around the edges. The petal shape minimizes diffraction.

faq.question: What is the Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope's coronagraph?
faq.answer: Roman will carry the first advanced coronagraph tested in space, designed to suppress starlight by factors of 100 million or more. It serves as a technology demonstration for future missions.
